questions.prompt: A deploy script without `set -e` runs `target="/srv/my app"` and then `cd $target`, followed by `tar -xzf release.tgz`. What happens?
choices: `cd` changes into `/srv/my app`, because a variable keeps its spaces
Bash refuses to start the script because a variable contains a space
`cd` receives two words, fails with `too many arguments`, and `tar` extracts into whatever directory the caller was in
`cd` changes into `/srv/my` and ignores the second word
questions.explanation: The unquoted expansion is split on IFS into `/srv/my` and `app`. `cd` fails, and without errexit the next line runs anyway, in the wrong directory. `cd "$target"` passes one word; `set -e` (or `cd ... || exit`) stops the script when it fails.

questions.prompt: Which of these expansions does Bash split on spaces and expand as a glob?
choices: `rm -f $tmpfile`, an argument of a simple command
`copy=$tmpfile`, the right side of an assignment
`[[ -f $tmpfile ]]`, inside double brackets
`case $tmpfile in *.tmp) ;; esac`, the case subject
questions.explanation: Splitting and globbing apply to unquoted expansions in the words of a command, `[ ]` included. Assignments, `[[ ]]`, the case subject, arithmetic and here-document bodies hold exactly one value, so Bash never splits there, and neither ShellCheck nor bashlint reports them.

questions.prompt: A script starts with `set -euo pipefail`. Which failing command does NOT stop it?
choices: `false` on a line of its own
`curl -fsS "$url" | tar -xz` when `curl` fails
`echo "$never_set"` when `never_set` was never assigned
`if grep -q ready status.txt; then ...` when `grep` finds nothing
questions.explanation: A command whose status is tested by `if`, `while`, `until`, `!` or the left side of `&&`/`||` is checked, so errexit leaves it alone. `false` alone exits, `pipefail` makes the pipeline fail when `curl` does, and `nounset` turns the unset variable into an error.

questions.prompt: bashlint reports BL008 (SC2115) for `rm -rf "$cache_dir/"*`. What is the right fix?
choices: Add `set -u`, which makes an empty variable an error
Write `rm -rf "${cache_dir:?}/"*`, so Bash stops with `cache_dir: parameter null or not set` before `rm` runs
Quote the star as well: `rm -rf "$cache_dir/*"`
Drop `-f` so `rm` asks before deleting
questions.explanation: `${var:?}` fails the expansion when the variable is unset or empty, so the command never runs. `set -u` only catches unset variables, not empty ones; a quoted star is a literal file name, not a glob; and `rm -r` without `-f` does not prompt for files it can write.

questions.prompt: The template `main.sh` runs `trap cleanup EXIT` before `WORK="$(mktemp -d)"`, and `cleanup` first checks `[[ -n "$WORK" ]]`. Why that order?
choices: Bash only allows a trap before the first command substitution
`mktemp` refuses to create a directory when no EXIT trap is set
It is only there to silence ShellCheck's SC2329
There is then no moment in which the directory exists and an exit would leave it behind, and the check makes `cleanup` safe if it runs before `mktemp` has assigned `WORK`
questions.explanation: If `mktemp` ran first, a signal or failure between it and the `trap` line would leak the directory. Setting the trap first closes that window; the emptiness check (with `${WORK:?}` in the `rm`) means an early exit never runs `rm -rf` on an empty path.

questions.prompt: A 40-line Bash script now has to call an HTTP API, retry `429` responses with backoff, read nested JSON, keep a map of results per host, and run on developers' Macs. What is the best move?
choices: Rewrite it in Python with `argparse`, `subprocess.run` with argument lists and timeouts for the commands it still needs, and the same arguments and exit codes
Add more `jq` calls and a `while` loop with `sleep` for the retries
Change the shebang to `#!/bin/sh` for portability
Add `set -x` so that failures are visible in the logs
questions.explanation: Retries with backoff, nested data, maps and testable logic are where Bash costs more than it saves, and macOS ships Bash 3.2 without associative arrays or `mapfile`. Keeping the CLI contract (arguments, exit codes, stdout for data, stderr for logs) lets callers switch without noticing.
